## Purpose

This SOP outlines the mandatory practices for securely and safely
handling, analyzing, and disposing of soils and sediments collected
from outside the United States. The importation and movement of
untreated foreign soil is classified by the USDA Animal and Plant
Health Inspection Service (APHIS) as an extremely high-risk activity
[@aphis_soil_import]. Several levels of review and approval are
required before a permit can be issued. This SOP has been written to
fulfill the conditions of the EA Program's APHIS foreign soil permit.

These practices are mandatory for all personnel working with foreign
soils in the EA Teaching and Research Laboratory at Pomona College.
Additionally, all persons working in the laboratory, even those not
directly handling foreign soils, must read this SOP and be aware of
standard operations involving quarantine materials so that a safe and
secure laboratory environment is maintained.


## Scope

- **Applies to:** All soils and sediments collected outside the United
  States and its territories that are imported to or processed in the
  EA Program laboratory
- **Does not apply to:** Domestic soils (including soils from Hawaii,
  Puerto Rico, and the U.S. Virgin Islands, which are not foreign
  countries under APHIS regulations); fully sterilized or commercially
  prepared soil reference materials
- **Analyses covered:** ICP-MS, EA-IRMS (total C, N, S and stable
  isotope ratios), texture, organic matter content, and other
  parameters where soils can be disposed of properly after analysis
- **Location:** Foreign soil storage in SGM 133 (designated cabinet);
  processing in SGM 134 (dedicated area)


## Responsibilities

| Role                  | Responsibility                                   |
|:----------------------|:-------------------------------------------------|
| PI (Permit Holder)    | Maintain active APHIS permit; ensure compliance  |
| Lab Manager           | Oversee quarantine storage; verify sterilization |
| Trained Personnel     | Handle soils per this SOP; log all activity      |
| All Lab Personnel     | Read this SOP; understand quarantine protocols even if not handling foreign soils |


## Definitions

- **APHIS (Animal and Plant Health Inspection Service):** The USDA
  agency responsible for protecting US agriculture from pests and
  diseases; regulates genetically engineered organisms and administers
  quarantine regulations; issues permits for importing soil and
  biological materials that could harbor plant pests or pathogens
  [@aphis_soil_import].
- **Autoclave sterilization:** Treatment of soil at 121 °C and 15 psi
  for at least 30--60 minutes to inactivate plant pathogens, weed
  seeds, nematodes, and other regulated organisms; required by USDA
  APHIS before foreign soil may be used in experiments outside a
  permitted facility.
- **CBP (U.S. Customs and Border Protection):** The federal agency
  that clears imported soils and plant material for entry into the
  United States, working alongside APHIS inspectors at Plant
  Inspection Stations.
- **Controlled import permit (PPQ Form 588):** A USDA APHIS document
  authorizing the importation of specified soil or biological material
  under defined containment and handling conditions; the PI must obtain
  this before any foreign soil enters the United States
  [@aphis_soil_import].
- **Decontamination:** A procedure that eliminates or reduces microbial
  contamination to a safe level with respect to transmission of
  infection; for foreign soils, typically achieved by autoclave or
  dry-heat sterilization.
- **Foreign soil:** Soil or sediment originating outside the United
  States and its territories; regulated by USDA APHIS under 7 CFR
  Part 330 because of the risk of introducing exotic plant pests,
  pathogens, and invasive species [@aphis_soil_import].
- **Permitted facility:** A laboratory or greenhouse that has been
  inspected and approved by USDA APHIS for work with imported soil or
  regulated biological materials; must meet physical containment
  requirements specified in the permit.
- **Plant Inspection Station (PIS):** A USDA/CBP facility at a port
  of entry where imported shipments are inspected and cleared by APHIS
  and CBP inspectors before release.
- **PPQ Form 508:** The green and yellow APHIS shipping label required
  for shipments of 3 lb or less that will be treated at the Plant
  Inspection Station.
- **PPQ Form 550:** The black and white APHIS shipping label required
  for shipments routed directly to a USDA-approved permitted facility.
- **Regulated article:** Any soil, plant material, or organism whose
  importation is controlled by USDA APHIS because of its potential to
  harbor or transmit plant pests or diseases.
- **ePermits:** The USDA APHIS online system for applying for and
  managing import permits and requesting shipping labels
  [@aphis_epermits].


## Safety and Hazards

::: {.callout-danger}
### APHIS Quarantine Requirement

Soil is strictly controlled under APHIS quarantine regulations 7 CFR
Part 330 because it can readily provide a pathway for introducing
dangerous organisms into the United States. Importation of soil from
foreign sources is prohibited unless authorized by APHIS under specific
conditions, safeguards, and controlled circumstances described in a
valid permit and/or compliance agreement. Noncompliance can result in
permit revocation, fines, and legal action [@aphis_soil_import].
:::

### Required PPE

- [ ] Standard laboratory coat
- [ ] Nitrile gloves
- [ ] Lab safety goggles
- [ ] Closed-toe shoes

### Storage Restrictions

- Foreign soils must be stored only in the designated quarantine
  cabinet in SGM 133
- Foreign soils must be processed only in the dedicated area in SGM 134
- Soils must never be opened or processed outside these designated
  areas

### Chemical Hazards

If chemicals are used during analysis (e.g., acids for digestion),
review the Safety Data Sheets before beginning. For isopropyl alcohol
used in decontamination, work in a well-ventilated area and keep away
from ignition sources.

### Emergency Procedures

Refer to
[SOP-L002 Laboratory Safety](SOP-L002-laboratory-safety.qmd)
and
[SOP-L003 Hazardous Materials Handling](SOP-L003-hazardous-materials-handling.qmd).
For spills of foreign soil, see §11 (Spill Cleanup).


## Personnel and Training Requirements

All personnel working with foreign soils must complete the following
before handling any quarantine material:

1. Complete [SOP-L002 Laboratory Safety](SOP-L002-laboratory-safety.qmd)
   training, including the annual Pomona College lab safety course
2. Read the USDA/APHIS Compliance Agreement (current agreement number
   on file with the PI)
3. Read the current Foreign Soil Permit (permit number on file with
   the PI) [@aphis_soil_import]
4. Read this SOP in full
5. Complete [SOP-L105 Drying Ovens](SOP-L105-drying-ovens.qmd)
   training (required for sterilization procedures)
6. Be signed off by the PI or lab manager

::: {.callout-important}
### All Lab Users
Even personnel who do not work directly with foreign soils must read
this SOP so they understand the quarantine protocols in effect in
SGM 133 and SGM 134. This is a condition of the APHIS permit.
:::

::: {.callout-note}
### APHIS Contact
For questions about the permit, shipping, or compliance, contact the
local APHIS Plant Protection and Quarantine office. Verify current
contact information with the PI before each import event, as personnel
assignments may change.
:::

## Sample Collection and Import

### Equipment Decontamination at the Collection Site

All field equipment must be thoroughly cleaned and disinfected of all
soil residues at the collection site before packing for transport.
Acceptable methods:

- Soak in isopropyl alcohol for one hour, or
- Soak and wash in hot water with detergent for 30 minutes

### Shipping Foreign Soils

1. Pack soil and sediment samples in sturdy, leak-proof containers.
   Declare contents as "Soil samples."
2. The primary container must be securely closed and watertight.
3. Enclose the primary container in a second, durable, watertight
   secondary container. Each container must be capable of containing
   the soil independently.
4. Attach the appropriate APHIS shipping label to the exterior of
   each shipping package [@aphis_soil_import]:
   - **PPQ Form 508** (green and yellow): For shipments of 3 lbs or
     less that will be treated at the PIS
   - **PPQ Form 550** (black and white): For shipments routed directly
     to the USDA-approved facility (Pomona College)

::: {.callout-warning}
### Label Placement
Packages without APHIS shipping labels on the exterior may be refused
entry even if labels are enclosed inside the package.
:::

5. Each label is individually numbered with a distinctive barcode.
   The permit holder must request the appropriate labels at the time
   of permit issuance.
6. Additional labels can be obtained through the "My Shipments/Labels"
   feature in ePermits [@aphis_epermits] or by emailing
   `BlackWhiteGreenYellowlabelrequest@aphis.usda.gov`.

### Waybills

- **PPQ Form 508 shipments** require two waybills: one international
  waybill to direct the shipment to the PIS, and one domestic waybill
  (placed inside the package) to direct the shipment from the PIS to
  the permit holder.
- **PPQ Form 550 shipments** require one waybill to direct the
  shipment to the permit holder.

The waybill must include: carrier account number or postage, permit
holder name, permit number, label number, delivery address, and
telephone number. If the waybill address does not match the permit
address, the package may be refused entry by CBP.

### Hand-Carrying Soils into the United States

Permitted articles may be hand-carried into the U.S. only if
[@aphis_soil_import]:

1. Hand carrying was requested in the permit application and
   authorized in the permit conditions
2. The permit conditions list the specific steps that must be followed
3. If someone other than the permit holder will hand-carry, that
   person must be identified on the permit
4. The authorized hand-carrier must follow all permit conditions
   pertaining to hand-carried shipments


## Receiving, Storage, and Logging

### Receiving

1. Transport soils directly to the Biogeochemistry Lab quarantine
   cabinet in SGM 133. Under no circumstances may soils be opened or
   processed until they reach the quarantine cabinet.
2. Open containers only inside the designated closed room area in
   SGM 133 or SGM 134. Take all precautions to prevent the escape of
   any potential pest that may be in the soil.

### Logging

Upon arrival at Pomona College, log every sample in the Foreign Soils
Log Book. Each entry must include:

| Field                    | Description                                    |
|:-------------------------|:-----------------------------------------------|
| Sample number            | Year and consecutive number (e.g., 18-01)      |
| Date of arrival          | YYYY-MM-DD                                     |
| Origin (provenance)      | Country, region, site name                     |
| Collector name/initials  | Who collected the sample in the field          |
| Mass (grams)             | As received                                    |
| Reason for collection    | Research project or study name                 |
| Storage location         | SGM 133 cabinet shelf, refrigerator, or freezer |
| Sterilization status     | Unsterilized (red tag) on arrival              |

### Labeling and Storage

1. Samples remain sealed in original Whirl-Pak bags within Ziplock
   bags until processed.
2. Store bags on shelf trays within the closed quarantine cabinet.
   Samples must not be left on tables or elsewhere when not in use.
3. All stored, unsterilized soils must be labeled with red tags
   stating "Quarantine Soil -- Unsterilized."
4. Sterilized samples must be labeled with green tags stating
   "Quarantine Soil -- Sterilized."
5. Any individual sample being processed outside its storage cabinet
   must also be clearly labeled to indicate sterilization status.


## Treatment, Sterilization, and Disposal

### Sterilization Method

Soil samples must be sterilized by dry heat treatment at 250 °C for
24 hours, or by one of the other approved methods documented in the
Foreign Soils Log Book.

::: {.callout-important}
### All Residues Must Be Sterilized
All residues from processing (including ash, rinse water filter
residues, and equipment rinse material) must be sterilized using the
same methods as the soil itself.
:::

### Disposal

After sterilization, soils may be disposed of in standard solid waste.
Document disposal date, mass, and method in the Foreign Soils Log Book.


## Mass Accounting and Audit

Periodically verify that the sum of all samples used in analyses and
the remaining inventory agrees with the original imported mass within
10% [@apha2012].

::: {.callout-note}
Discrepancies exceeding 10% must be investigated and documented.
:::


## Quality Control

- Verify that the APHIS Foreign Soil Permit is current and has not
  expired before any import activity.
- Confirm that APHIS shipping labels match the current permit number.
- Audit the Foreign Soils Log Book at least once per semester to
  verify all entries are complete and mass accountability is within
  10% [@apha2012].
- Report any anomalies (missing samples, mass discrepancies, permit
  questions) to the PI immediately.

## Training Record

Before handling foreign soils independently, personnel must:

1. Read this SOP in full
2. Complete [SOP-L002 Laboratory Safety](SOP-L002-laboratory-safety.qmd)
   training
3. Complete [SOP-L105 Drying Ovens](SOP-L105-drying-ovens.qmd)
   training
4. Read the current APHIS Compliance Agreement and Foreign Soil Permit
   (copies on file with the PI) [@aphis_soil_import]
5. Complete the annual Pomona College lab safety course
6. Demonstrate proper logging, labeling (red/green tags), and
   sterilization procedures under supervision
7. Be signed off by the PI


## Appendix A: Sample Numbering Convention {.appendix}

Each sample receives a number consisting of the two-digit year and a
consecutive number for that year. For example, 18-34 indicates the
34th sample logged in 2018. The numbering resets to 01 at the start
of each calendar year.
